item.title: El Salvador's president confirms and celebrates attack on home of key Haitian gang leader
item.description:
El Salvador's president confirms and celebrates attack on home of key Haitian gang leader
El Salvador’s president says that his troops have demolished the lavish home of a prominent gang leader in Haiti known as JeffByDÁNICA COTO Associated PressNovember 18, 2026, 10:35 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico -- El Salvador’s president, Nayib Bukele, said Wednesday that his troops demolished the lavish home of a prominent gang leader in Haiti known as Jeff. It wasn’t immediately clear if he was killed.
Bukele posted a video on X that depicts an old video of Jeff posing in front of his mansion in the Caribbean country and then cuts to Salvadoran helicopters flying toward it as they fire shot after shot, with big plumes of smoke rising from Jeff’s home.
“My gift to the Haitian people on the anniversary of the Battle of Vertières,” Bukele wrote.
The 1803 battle was critical in helping secure Haiti's independence from France and transforming it into the world's first Black republic.
It wasn’t immediately known if Haiti’s police and army were involved. A U.N.-backed gang suppression force said that it wasn’t involved.
Jeff is considered one of Haiti's most powerful gang leaders. His real name is Jeff Larose, but he's known as Jeff Canaan, Jeff Gwo Lwa and Taliban. He has long controlled a community known as Canaan in northern Port-au-Prince, leading a gang of an estimated 200 members, according to the United Nations. His so-called Taliban gang based in Canaan is a very close ally of 5 Segond, which has provided it with reinforcements.
Diego Da Rin, a Haiti expert with International Crisis Group, said the attack on Jeff’s home was the obvious next step for Bukele’s operations.
Jeff built the home in mid-2024, complete with a pool emblazoned with his logo.
“It’s very easy to identify it by satellite,” Da Rin said. “It was a very defiant act by him.”

item.title: A Chinese executive is convicted in a case linked to a Bangkok building collapse
item.description:
A Chinese executive is convicted in a case linked to a Bangkok building collapse
A Thai court has found a Chinese executive and Thai shareholders guilty of illegally operating a business in ThailandByJINTAMAS SAKSORNCHAI Associated PressNovember 18, 2026, 10:56 AM
Share
BANGKOK -- A court in Thailand on Wednesday found a Chinese executive and Thai shareholders of a Thai subsidiary of a Chinese state-owned construction company guilty of illegally operating a business in Thailand in a case related to the collapse of a Bangkok office building last year.
At least 92 people died on March 28, 2025, when an earthquake struck the partially built high-rise, which was to house the State Audit Office. It was the only building in Thailand to collapse completely due to the 7.7-magnitude quake, which was centered in neighboring Myanmar.
The tower was being built by a joint venture between China Railway No. 10 (Thailand) and Italian-Thai Development. Executives from both companies are also facing separate proceedings over alleged wrongdoing related to the building’s collapse.
China Railway No. 10 (Thailand) and its director, Zhang Chuanling, were found guilty of violating Thailand’s Foreign Business Act by using Thai nominee shareholders to conceal the company’s foreign ownership and operating a construction business without the required permission. The Criminal Court in Bangkok fined the company and Zhang 1 million baht ($29,450) each and sentenced Zhang to three years in prison, while also ordering the company to cease operations.
The defendants had denied the charges and were granted bail.
China Railway No. 10 (Thailand) is a Thai-registered affiliate of China Railway No. 10 Engineering Group, part of the Chinese state-owned China Railway group, which operates internationally.

item.title: A cyberattack using artificial intelligence targeted the EU in October, official says
item.description:
A cyberattack using artificial intelligence targeted the EU in October, official says
An official in Brussels says a cyberattack using software powered by artificial intelligence targeted the European Union in OctoberByThe Associated PressNovember 19, 2026, 7:30 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
BRUSSELS -- A cyberattack carried out with artificial intelligence targeted the European Union in October, an official in Brussels said on Thursday, and some of the bloc's digital tools remain offline.
The official did not elaborate on the cyberattack, or say who could have been behind it. It was the first time the 27-member bloc reported a cyberattack using an AI tool.
“AI-assisted tools can be used and especially misused to detect vulnerabilities," said Thomas Regnier, spokesperson for the European Commission, the executive body of the 27-nation EU.
"Indeed we can confirm that this was done with AI tools," he added. "We have seen many global cyberattacks recently, and of course no one is immune to this.”
Regnier said the EU first detected the incident on Oct. 22 and that authorities launched an investigation while also imposing “preventative measures."

item.title: Japan, India agree to enhance military and defense industry cooperation
item.description:
Japan, India agree to enhance military and defense industry cooperation
Japan and India have agreed to enhance their military and arms industry cooperation, including allowing Japanese troops to conduct live-fire missile training at Indian firing ranges in future joint drillsByMARI YAMAGUCHI Associated PressNovember 19, 2026, 9:22 AM
TOKYO -- TOKYO (AP) — Japan and India agreed to enhance their military and arms industry cooperation, including allowing Japanese troops to conduct live-fire missile training at Indian firing ranges in future joint drills, as their defense and foreign ministers met Thursday in Tokyo.
Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi and Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi joined their Indian counterparts, Rajnath Singh and S. Jaishankar, at the “two-plus-two" meeting in Tokyo.
The two Asian powers have been rapidly deepening security, defense and economic ties in recent years amid growing tension and uncertainty in the region. India and Japan also are part of the Quad grouping with the United States and Australia that aims to counter China’s influence.
“Through our cooperation, we hope to serve as the anchor for the Indo-Pacific region,” Motegi told a joint news conference after the talks.
This defense industrial cooperation will proceed under the framework of “design with Japan, make in India,” Singh said.
As an island nation with limited space to safely conduct missile tests and training, Japan needs defense partners that can provide facilities for its military to practice live-fire drills essential to improving missile capability. Japan struck a similar arrangement with Australia this year.

item.title: Trump, Xi and Putin hold rare 3-way talks on nuclear risks but emerge with no major breakthroughs
item.description:
Trump, Xi and Putin hold rare 3-way talks on nuclear risks but emerge with no major breakthroughs
Three leaders who view their nations as the world’s superpowers have sat around a table together for the first time to talk about reducing nuclear risks and resolving conflictsByJOSH BOAK Associated Press, MICHELLE L. PRICE Associated Press, and E. EDUARDO CASTILLO Associated PressNovember 18, 2026, 8:00 PM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
SHENZHEN, China -- Three leaders who view their nations as the world's superpowers sat around a table together for the first time on Thursday to talk about reducing nuclear risks and resolving conflicts — a step they applauded as historic though they did not agree to any major breakthroughs.
U.S. President Donald Trump, China’s Xi Jinping and Russia’s Vladimir Putin offered smiles and friendly handshakes, ending their talks at a villa in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen by agreeing on points including U.N. reforms and a vow to get more fuel to the market. It remains to be seen if the gathering could mark a pivot in world history — or become a quickly forgotten photo op.
The leaders made only brief remarks at the beginning and didn't take questions afterward, releasing a short statement that did not mention the wars in Ukraine or Iran, two issues that Trump said he raised with the leaders in separate one-on-ones earlier in the day.
The agreements were modest, but the rhetoric was not.
“We are really making history,” Trump said. “The United States, Russia and China are uniquely positioned to discuss how to reduce the number of nuclear weapons on Earth and also to lessen the risk of those weapons being used."
Xi earlier said the meeting would focus on “promoting world peace.” Putin, for his part, said the countries “hold joint responsibility for maintaining international peace.”

item.title: Brazil's Senate approves Lula's $10 billion fiscal package after costly election spending
item.description:
Brazil's Senate approves Lula's $10 billion fiscal package after costly election spending
Brazil’s Senate approved on Wednesday a plan by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva to control his government’s spending and increase revenues after his reelection late OctoberByMAURICIO SAVARESE Associated PressNovember 18, 2026, 5:56 PM
SAO PAULO -- SAO PAULO (AP) — Brazil 's Senate approved on Wednesday a plan by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva to control his government’s spending and increase revenues after his reelection late October led market analysts to worry about Brazil’s economy. The 81-year-old leader came back with a series of incentives to voters after losing the first round of voting to Flávio Bolsonaro.
The Brazilian government’s fiscal package, which will also have to be approved by the lower house, introduces new rules to slow down the growth of spending, limits corporate tax breaks and closes loopholes. It seeks to improve the ‌public finances by up to 60 billion reais (about $10 billion) next year.
Lula’s move is laying bare the challenges ahead of his fourth nonconsecutive administration, as it already has many critics left and right. Many of his supporters see the plan as a risk to welfare programs, while his critics among market agents deem it to be too shy.
Many analysts say Lula's fiscal package is too dependent on boosting revenues rather than cutting expenses. That perception has led to the depreciation of Brazilian assets in recent days, including the country's real currency. Lula is yet to announce who will be his finance minister for the new term.
Lula’s victories in 2002 and 2022 also sparked immediate depreciation of Brazilian assets, but stock markets eventually recovered from high losses.

item.title: Pakistan military says it killed 22 militants in raids on hideouts in northwest
item.description:
Pakistan military says it killed 22 militants in raids on hideouts in northwest
Pakistan's military says security forces have raided militant hideouts in the northwest near the Afghan border, setting off gunbattles that killed 22 militantsByThe Associated PressNovember 19, 2026, 2:21 AM
ISLAMABAD -- Pakistani security forces acting on intelligence raided militant hideouts in the northwest near the Afghan border, setting off gunbattles that killed 22 militants, the military said Thursday.
It alleged that the militants killed were backed by neighboring India. There was no immediate comment from New Delhi, but Pakistan often accuses Afghanistan and India of supporting the Pakistani Taliban and other militant groups, allegations both countries deny.
The raids took place over the past 48 hours in the South Waziristan, Bannu and Tank districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, the military said in a statement.
The military reported last week that security forces had killed 74 militants over several days in raids on hideouts in the northwest and in southwestern Balochistan province.
The military said troops were searching the areas for any remaining militants and pledged to continue operations against what it described as foreign-backed terrorism.

item.title: Fire set at home of former Bangladesh interim leader as political tensions rise
item.description:
Fire set at home of former Bangladesh interim leader as political tensions rise
Authorities in Bangladesh say a fire at the ancestral home of a former Bangladesh interim leader and Nobel Peace Prize laureate appears to have been intentionally setByJULHAS ALAM Associated PressNovember 19, 2026, 3:10 AM
Share
DHAKA, Bangladesh -- A late-night fire at the ancestral home of a former Bangladesh interim leader and Nobel Peace Prize laureate appeared to have been intentionally set, police said.
The fire occurred as growing waves of violence and damage have followed a declaration by the ousted former prime minister, Sheikh Hasina, that she plans to return to the country soon from exile.
The fire occurred before midnight Wednesday at the home of Muhammad Yunus, who served as interim leader of the country for 18 months following a mass uprising that led to the ouster of Hasina, who was flown out of the country by the military on Aug. 5, 2024.
The fire in an abandoned, ground-floor room of Yunus' house in Chattogram was spotted by a police patrol that immediately doused the flames, Police Inspector Mozammel Haque told local media Thursday. Police are investigating and additional details were not immediately available.
The possible arson comes during ongoing political tensions following an announcement by Hasina she intends to end her exile in India in December. In an interview with The Associated Press earlier this month, Hasina said even death cannot prevent her from returning to Bangladesh.
Hasina has requested a passport and national identity card to facilitate her return, but the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party led by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman insists she will not receive the documents and must be handed over by India under an extradition treaty.

item.title: Denmark approves security deal with US and Greenland, seeking to finally ease tensions with Trump
item.description:
Denmark approves security deal with US and Greenland, seeking to finally ease tensions with Trump
Denmark’s parliament has approved an agreement with Greenland and the United States to strengthen security in the Arctic and North AtlanticByThe Associated PressNovember 19, 2026, 4:41 AM
COPENHAGEN, Denmark -- Denmark’s parliament on Thursday approved a hard-wrought deal with Greenland and the United States to strengthen security in the Arctic and North Atlantic, a final step aimed to defuse months of tensions over the Trump administration's pressure about a possible U.S. takeover of the vast, mineral-rich island.
The trilateral deal — between U.S. President Donald Trump and Danish and Greenlandic leaders — paves the way for more U.S. bases in Greenland, a semiautonomous territory of NATO ally Denmark. It also eases tensions in the Atlantic alliance and with the European Union over Trump’s repeated calls for the vast island to become part of the U.S.
The 109-0 vote in the Folketing amounts to a final step: The deal enters into force once the parliaments of Denmark and Greenland have signed on, followed by formal notification of the United States in a diplomatic note.
Greenland’s parliament approved the deal earlier this month, also with no opposition.
“Today is a big day,” Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen wrote on Facebook. “It hasn’t been an easy process.”
She said the agreement respects Denmark's sovereignty and territorial integrity, and the right of Greenlanders to self-determination.
Greenlandic Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen wrote on Facebook that Thursday's vote proved that Greenlanders can stand firm in their rights while also finding solutions through dialogue and cooperation.
“We have been through a difficult time, during which many people here at home have been concerned about our country and our future,” he said. “I hope that today’s decision will help bring greater calm and a sense of security.”

item.title: Iran war dents Middle East sports as events are canceled. F1 bucks the trend
item.description:
Iran war dents Middle East sports as events are canceled. F1 bucks the trend
The season-ending Formula 1 races in the Middle East are going ahead despite the war in Iran and retaliatory attacks across the region that have canceled or postponed other large sports eventsBySTEPHEN WADE AP sports writerNovember 18, 2026, 12:07 AM
Two season-ending Formula 1 races in the Middle East are going ahead despite the war in Iran and retaliatory attacks across the region that have canceled or postponed other large sports events. This includes two Formula 1 races earlier this year in Saudi Arabia and Bahrain.
The conflict has upended the region's image as a safe haven where governments and sponsors have kicked in billions to lure mega-sports events. This comes as Europe and North America appear wary of such lavish spending.
“The situation could change but the geography will not change,” Sebastian Sons, who follows sports in the Middle East with the German research institute CARPO, told The Associated Press. “The Middle East and the Gulf region are always a volatile and fragile region.”
Going ahead is an endorsement for doing business in the region, but has also prompted concerns about safety from some teams and staff. Mohammed Ben Sulayem, the president of auto racing's world governing body FIA, has said “we are fully prepared” to pull off the two races: Qatar on Nov. 29 and Abu Dhabi on Dec. 6.
Ben Sulayem is from the United Arab Emirates.
A MotoGP race was held in Qatar on Nov. 8 on the track where F1 races. MotoGP is operated by Liberty Media, which also runs F1.
“Holding the races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi signals that those two are stable and able to host large-scale sporting events. It is important they are seen to be open for business,” Kristian Ulrichsen, a political scientist at Rice University's Baker Institute, told The AP.
